Up before the cock, {title}? Fair morning.
Well met at midday, {title}. The sun is high.
Evening, {title}. The day is nearly done.
Late to be abroad, {title}. What brings you out?
I do not know your face. Welcome to {place}, {title}.
A new face. Be welcome, though keep to the road.
{name}, is it not? Good to see you.
{name}! Sit, sit; the ale is fresh.
There you are, {name}. I was just speaking of you.
My friend {name}. What news with you?
{name}. For you the door is always open.
Come in out of it, {name}. You know you need not ask.
You again. Be quick about it.
You have a nerve, showing your face.
Mm. Good day. I am not in the best of humour.
Oh. It is you. Well, good day.
A fine day, {title}, a fine day indeed!
Ha! Good to see a friendly face. Good day!
Long day in the {field_or_yard}, {title}. Mind the mud.
Fair day for the work, {title}. Stand clear of the barrow.
Mind the shop, {title}; I have work laid out.
Good day. Keep the peace and we shall get on.
Wet weather, {title}. Come under the eave a moment.
Half drowned, are we? Good day all the same, {title}.
Cold enough for you, {title}? Good day.
Cousin! I had not looked for you. Come, come.
Come by the fire again soon, {name}.
Walk carefully, {name}. I would not lose you.
Mind the door on your way out.
Keep to the lit streets, {title}. Goodnight.
Mind the mud. May you find a dry roof by dark.
Off with you, then, and God speed!
Clear sky today. A good day for the work.
Not a cloud. I could not ask for better.
Grey and heavy. Rain by evening, I would wager.
The sky is low today. It presses on a man.
A soft rain. It will do the fields good.
Drizzle again. The ford will be up by noon.
Rain again. The ford will be up by noon, and the roads worse.
Not a day to be on the road. The mud takes a cart to the axle.
That thunder is close. I do not like it near the barns.
A storm like this takes a roof or two, mark me.
Thick fog. I could lose my own hand in it.
Fog on the water. The ferryman will not cross until it lifts.
Frost on the fields; the winter wheat will be glad.
Hard frost. The well rope is stiff as a bone.
Snow again. The lanes will be closed by morning.
Pretty, snow, if you have wood stacked. I have not enough.
Nobody should be out in this. Get yourself indoors.
I have known a blizzard bury a sheepfold whole.
This heat. The ale turns in the barrel before it is drunk.
Too hot to work and too dry to rest. The wells are low.
A cold {season}. Stack the wood before you need it.
Rain in {season} is a blessing for the barley.
Ploughing and sowing; there is no rest in {season}.
The lambs are coming. I have not slept a full night in a week.
Long days of {season}. We work them all.
The harvest is everything. Pray the weather holds.
Every barn is filling. The mice are fat this year.
Winter is long. We count the barley to the grain.
Short days, long nights. I mend what I can by the fire.
A feast day. The brewer has been at it since dawn.
Feast day! Even the miller will lay down his sack.
The {feast} is in {days} {#days|day|days}. The brewer is counting barrels already.
Only {days} {#days|day|days} until {feast}. I have not even begun to prepare.
The barley wants rain, and so do I.
Tithe, rent and seed corn; the field feeds everyone but the man who ploughs it.
A straight furrow takes patience, and a good ox.
My hands know the plough better than they know my own wife.
The flock was restless last night. Wolves, perhaps.
A good dog is worth three boys, and eats less.
The stream is low and the stones are slow. People grumble, but I cannot make water.
Every sack gets the toll, and every man thinks I take too much.
The oven wants wood and the dough wants time; nothing hurries bread.
Flour has gone dear. I will not make the loaves smaller, but I may have to.
A good ale is patience and clean barrels. Folk forget the second.
The barley price is up, and my customers expect the same cup for the same coin.
The best cuts go to the lord. The rest is honest meat.
A cold snap is the butcher's friend. Nothing spoils.
A good edge starts with good iron, and iron has been dear.
The forge eats charcoal like a hungry dog, and charcoal is not cheap.
Seasoned oak is worth more than gold to a carpenter. Green wood warps.
Everyone wants a roof; no one wants to wait for it.
Stone remembers. A bad wall leans for a hundred years.
Mortar will not set in this cold. The work stops until it warms.
The loom does not hurry, and neither do I. Good cloth takes its time.
Wool is short this year. I am working with what I have.
You will smell my trade before you see it. The work is honest, though.
Hides, bark, lime, patience. Leather is more a waiting than a working.
A good boot is half the road. I mend more than I make.
Wet feet make a bad day. Come to me before the rains.
Prices rise at one end of the road and fall at the other. That is all trade is.
A caravan late is a month of worry. I count the days.
A full taproom is a loud one, but I will not complain of the coin.
Travellers bring news and trouble in equal parts.
The Lord provides, though He does not always provide quickly.
The harvest is His gift, and I remind them to give thanks for it.
Quiet watch. Quiet is good; I get paid the same either way.
Cold feet, empty belly; yet someone must watch the gate.
The river gives and the river takes. I only cast the net.
Pike are running thin this year. I blame the weir.
My eldest is courting the miller's girl. I pretend not to notice.
We have a babe at home. Nobody sleeps, but nobody minds.
My back is not what it was. Thirty years of bending will do that.
My knees tell me the weather before the sky does.
Blood is blood. Family comes first, whatever else.
Mother always said I would end up like my uncle. She was right.
The market has been busy. Folk are buying more than they ought.
The reeve is in a mood. Say nothing to him about the fences.
The well water tastes odd lately. I boil what I drink.
Neighbours: you cannot pick them. I have the best and the worst on one side.
The dog has taken against the cat. They are both hateful and both mine.
There is an old feud over a boundary stone. Nobody remembers who moved it.
Everything costs more than last year. Wages do not.
Taxes, taxes. The lord takes his due before the harvest is in.
I light a candle for the dead on feast days. It helps, a little.
The children have been into the apples again. I cannot blame them.
Eighty winters I have seen. I do not remember a colder one.
They sing a new song at the tavern. It is terrible, and I know every word.
I sleep badly. The owl on the roof is no help.
Things will mend. They always do, somehow.
I need {goods} carried to {place} by {day_name}. {price} for it. Interested?
Take this to {place} and you will have {price}. There is no hurry, but do not dawdle.
Nothing today, but ask the reeve.
Not a thing, I am afraid. Try again after the harvest.
Hands wanted in the {field_or_yard}. {price} a day, and a bowl at noon.
I could use a strong back at the hay. {price}, paid at dusk.
Every hand is wanted for the harvest. {price} a day, and you eat with us.
Hold this a moment. Now carry it to the shop door. {price} for the trouble.
I need charcoal fetched from the burners. {price} if you are quick.
Wood for the oven, a cartload. {price}, and a loaf besides.
Barrels to roll to the tavern. {price}, and an ale when the work is done.
Watch the flock tonight and you shall have {price}. Bring a cloak.
The cellar wants clearing. {price}, and a hot meal after.
I need a hand for the road to {place}. {price}, and you eat well.
Watch needs more feet. {price} a night, and the cold is free.
Fuel is short. Split wood for me and I will pay {price}.
For you, {name}, there is always something. {price}, and no questions.
If you want work, {name}, I have some. {price} is fair, I think.
I do not know you. I will not hand you coin before I see your work.
Work? Everyone wants work. Go ask the reeve.
{price} the {unit}. That is what it fetches at {place}, as I hear.
{price} the {unit}, and I am not robbing you.
The stock is thin. Come again in a few days.
It is dear this season, {title}; I did not set the price, the weather did.
Plenty about, so cheap. Buy now, before I think better of it.
For a friend, {price} the {unit}. Do not tell the others.
You may have it at cost, {name}. I trust you will remember me.
New face, so full price: {price} the {unit}.
I will sell to you, but at {price} and not a mite less.
I do not sell to your sort.
Bread is {price} the loaf; fresh this morning.
Day-old at half price, if you do not mind the crust.
Nails, hinges, blades; name it. {price} for good iron.
The edge is honest. It will hold, if you do not abuse it.
Ale is {price} the cup. Strong, or small, as you like.
Fresh meat, {price} the {unit}. Ask for the offal if you are thrifty.
Cloth, salt, spices; everything has a price. Let us talk.
What I have, I sell. What I do not have, I can find, for a fee.
This cloth is {price} the ell. Feel the weave; none better in {place}.
Boots to measure, {price}. A week to make them, no sooner.
Hides, {price} each. They will last a lifetime, if you oil them.
A bed is {price} a night; supper, a little more.
Flour is {price} the {unit}. The toll is the toll.
Barley, {price} the {unit}. I would rather sell to a neighbour than the market.
You drive a hard bargain, {title}. Make it a little more and we are done.
Is that your best? Come now, you are not at a fair.
Ha! You know the trade. {price}, and not a mite less.
I have a family to feed, {title}. I cannot go lower.
A deal. May it do us both good.
I have not the coin to buy it from you, I am afraid.
{price} a day, and food? I will carry your pack.
{price} a day and a roof, and I am yours until the job is done.
I am promised elsewhere this week, sorry.
Since it is you, {name}, I will take it, and for less.
I do not know you. Pay me up front, and I might think about it.
If there is fighting in it, the price doubles and I want it in advance.
Soldiering is not my trade. Ask someone with a spear.
I know my trade. {price} a day, and you will not be disappointed.
Food and a place by the fire, and I will take less. Winter is coming.
I will work for bread, if you have it.
I will go for {price}, if it keeps my family fed.
Well, I have nothing better to do. Lead on.
The road is better than another winter here. Count me in.
Aye, I will go with you. I have been waiting for a reason to leave.
We hardly know each other, {name}. Give it time.
I do not trust you well enough to follow you into trouble.
What would I gain by going? You have not told me why I should.
You have a full company already, {title}. Come to me when there is room.
You cannot pay me; I will not join an empty purse.
For you, {name}, I would walk to the world's end.
You are blood, {name}. Of course I will come.
I am too old for the road now. Ask the young ones.
I have my own to think of. Do not ask it of me.
The signing bonus is generous, I will say that.
Take the north road past the mill; {place} is about {n} {#n|hour|hours} on foot.
East, by the old ford. {place} is {n} {#n|hour|hours} away on a good day.
South along the river; {place} lies about {n} {#n|hour|hours} on.
Out the west gate. {place} is {n} {#n|hour|hours}, and the road is rough.
{place}? A long way. Take food, and do not walk it at night.
{place} is just beyond the rise. You cannot miss it.
The smithy is by the green; follow the sound of the hammer.
The tavern is on the square. Look for the sign with the crooked boar.
The church is at the top of the lane. The bell can be heard from everywhere.
The market is on the square. Go early, the best goods go first.
You look lost, {title}. Where do you want to go?
The low road floods in rain. Take the high one, even if it is longer.
I would not travel to {place} after dark. Wait for morning.
I have never been there. Ask someone who has.
I saw it with my own eyes: {rumour}
I was there. {rumour} I will not forget it soon.
You want the truth? Here it is, and I saw it: {rumour}
Not a tale, {title}; I saw it. {rumour}
I had it from {teller}, who is not one to lie: {rumour}
It is all over the lane: {rumour}
I heard it at the well, and who knows who from. {rumour}
A traveller told it at the tavern: {rumour}
Word came up the road from {place}. {rumour}
I hear it was worse than that, though. {rumour}
Who knows how true it is, but they say {rumour}
The story grows with the telling, but the gist is this: {rumour}
Do not hold me to the details. {rumour}
Hunger is a hard thing to talk about. {rumour}
Not safe on the roads these days. {rumour}
Keep clear of the sick, and pray. {rumour}
A wicked deed, and no one punished yet. {rumour}
War is a rich man's game and a poor man's burden. {rumour}
The lord wants his share, and then some. {rumour}
Everything is dear, and about to get dearer. {rumour}
Folk are building, which is a good sign, I suppose. {rumour}
Nothing I would repeat, {title}. Ask me in a few days.
Keep your hand off that sword while you talk to me.
You are covered in blood. I will not stand near you.
What have you done? Do not come near my children.
It is the middle of the night. Come back in daylight.
I have no time. Ask someone else.
Later, {title}. I am up to my elbows in work.
I do not talk business with strangers.
You look rich. Whatever you want, I cannot afford it.
I have nothing to say to you.
I do not talk to your sort.
Leave, or I call the watch.
State your business or move along.
I am sorry, {title}; I cannot help with that.
One more step and you will regret it.
Scum. Get out of my sight.
I have not eaten since yesterday, {title}.
I would talk, but my belly is louder than I am.
I would talk, but my feet ache.
I could sleep on my feet, {title}. Forgive me.
Forgive me; I am half frozen. Can we talk by a fire?
My hands are numb. I cannot even hold the cup.
I am not well. Do not stand too close.
A fever, and no money for the apothecary.
Have a drink with me, friend! I am a happy drunk.
You are all blurry. Hold still.
Everything is going wrong this week. Forgive my tongue.
My heart is not in it today. What do you need?
I could sing! I am in good spirits today.
Life is good, {title}. I mean to enjoy it.
We buried my kin not long ago. Be gentle with me.
You look well-fed, {title}. Some of us are not.
Hup, hup! Back in the fold!
The oven is hot. Get the dough in.
Burnt again? Not on my watch.
A little more malt in this one.
Mind the cleaver, mind the cleaver.
Strike while the iron is hot!
Another blade for the lord, and no thanks for it.
Another ell, and I am done.
Hides on the line, mind the smell.
Tap, tap, tap. A boot is not made in a day.
Awl and thread, awl and thread.
Mend the net, mend the net.
Fresh bread, hot from the oven!
Ale, cold ale, a farthing the cup!
Salt! Good salt from the coast!
Come, come, the best prices in the market!
Mend your pots! Mend your pots!
Boots, solid boots for the road!
Not a cloud. Good drying weather.
What a day! I could work till dark.
This rain will drown the seedlings.
I cannot see my own feet in this.
Frost on the well rope again.
Hot enough to bake the bread in the street.
Lights out, citizens. Curfew is on.
Keep to the lit streets, friend.
All is well on the wall.
Quiet now. Good folk are sleeping.
A rooster crows, late and proud.
What is he planning with that blade?
God above, he is covered in blood!
Fetch the watch! There has been a killing.
A rich one, by the look of that purse.
Fine boots. Coin to burn, that one.
Who is that? A new face.
That is the one folk are talking about.
Bread is dearer again, and the coin no thicker.
Look at that price! It is robbery.
The tax-man was round again. Taxes, taxes.
They will have the shirt off my back before winter.
My belly is as empty as a drum.
Has anyone a crust to spare?

{who} of {place} is dead, and not by the hand of God.
{who} of {place} was carried off by a fever, aged {number}.
{number} folk rioted at {place} over the price of grain.

a caravan has gone missing near {about}.
plague has come to {about}, and people are fleeing.

{number} acres have been cleared for the plough at {place}.

though I could not tell you where
You have the look of someone who wants to be somewhere else. I am Marta Voss, and I run the wagons out of {place}. What do you want?
I can ride. What would that earn me?
Work, is it? I have a wagon of salt for the coast road and one hand short. The pay is fair and the journey is a long one. Can you walk beside a cart for a week?
Yes. I will take the job.
Food on the road, a bed in the wagon, and a day's wage for every day, paid at the end. A good hand might earn a share of the profit, if the salt arrives dry.
Dangerous enough. There are bandits in the woods past the ford, and the weather is as bad as ever. I have never lost a wagon, mind. I take care.
I will take it all the same.
Good. Here is a lantern; a man who carries his own light is worth two. We leave at first light. Do not be late.
Eat something. You will need it.
My father drove wagons, and his father before him. The road is in our blood. I have never owned a field, and I never wanted one.
I was nine when I first drove the team. I fell off and broke my wrist, and the wagon did not even stop. My father said that was the best lesson I would ever have.
A husband in {place}, two sons who think wagons are boring. They are right, in a way, and I would not have it differently.
Depends where. Highways are dry and dull; tracks are mud and trouble. And one bad ford can cost you a day.
In the woods past the ford, mostly. A few of them were farmers once, which makes them worse. They like narrow places and tired travellers.
When it rains, the ford is up to a man's chest. Wait for it to fall; I have seen a cart carried off with the oxen still in the traces.
Walk in daylight, camp early, keep a fire. Never sleep with your boots off. And pay the toll without argument; a quarrel costs more than a coin.
